headline: How Sperm Whales Master the Art of Resting Upright
meta_description: Scientists confirm sperm whales release bubbles to stay neutrally buoyant while resting vertically underwater, a unique behavior studied over 14 years.
summary_short: Researchers tracking 42 sperm whales near Norway discovered how these marine giants release air bubbles to maintain their signature vertical resting position.
body:
Sperm whales possess one of the ocean's most unusual rest habits: they float perfectly still in a vertical position, suspended just below the surface like underwater statues. Scientists have now confirmed what researchers long suspected—that these whales deliberately release bubbles to maintain this precarious balance. Using data collected between 2005 and 2019 from 42 whales tagged near Norway's Lofoten Islands, researchers identified 17 whales engaged in this resting behavior, which lasted anywhere from minutes to three hours at a stretch.

The mechanism behind this feat is elegant. Sperm whales possess a massive, oil-filled organ in their heads called the spermaceti organ—a waxy substance lighter than water that naturally buoys them. As whales drift upward in this vertical rest position, the expanding air in their lungs pushes them further toward the surface. By releasing bubbles, they counteract this upward force, staying submerged without expending energy to swim. Lead researcher Noémie Freymond from Switzerland's Université de Neuchâtel emphasized that while the vertical resting position had been observed for years, this study provided the first systematic documentation of how bubble release actually regulates buoyancy.

The discovery carries unexpected significance for whale conservation. Understanding how sperm whales rest and maintain awareness during these vulnerable periods could help scientists assess their susceptibility to human threats, particularly ship strikes. The research also reveals that whales adjust their breathing patterns during rest compared to active dives—suggesting they respond dynamically to environmental changes even while resting. This adaptive behavior hints at depths of whale intelligence and physiology we're only beginning to understand.
quick_facts: 42 sperm whales tagged near Norway's Lofoten Islands between 2005–2019
17 whales recorded resting vertically, lasting minutes to three hours
Spermaceti organ in whale head provides natural buoyancy via waxy oil
Bubble release counteracts upward pressure from expanding lung air
Study first to systematically document bubble-buoyancy regulation mechanism
